summary:
cmcr-1423444 1.1.0 is a ward case about a 63-year-old man with hepatitis B cirrhosis. His back pain and worsening walking had been treated as a lumbar disc problem. Files: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ClinicalCraft/61c17a21-a923-5d20-a08c-1c8a508459b0/scratchpad/pr5/wt/packages/content/cases/cmcr-1423444/case.json and README.md. Builder scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ClinicalCraft/61c17a21-a923-5d20-a08c-1c8a508459b0/scratchpad/work-cmcr-1423444/.

WHAT IT TEACHES:
(1) Localisation. Increased leg tone, brisk knee reflexes, bilateral Babinski and Hoffmann signs, urinary incontinence and a tight, bound chest point to a spinal cord lesion at the cervical cord or above, not a lumbar disc. The next step is urgent MRI of the cervical and thoracic cord plus blood and urine tests for metabolic and drug causes (NICE NG59 2016).
(2) The tubular picture. Glycosuria at a fasting glucose of 4.5 mmol/L, alpha-1 microglobulin 257.8 mg/L, NAG 90 U/L, phosphate 0.37 mmol/L and urate 122 μmol/L make a proximal tubulopathy (Fanconi syndrome). A creatinine of 119 μmol/L hides it (EASL 2025). The likeliest cause is adefovir taken for 5½ years (Hepsera label 2018: delayed nephrotoxicity, Fanconi syndrome, osteomalacia).
(3) The antiviral. Switch the same day, never pause. Use entecavir if he never had lamivudine, otherwise TAF. Drug and dose depend on liver compensation and renal function (EASL 2025; Chinese guideline 2022).
(4) Bone and phosphate. Give oral phosphate with active vitamin D after checking albumin-adjusted calcium, magnesium, PTH and vitamin D. Do not give a bisphosphonate or an NSAID.
(5) Causality. On WHO-UMC, a positive dechallenge makes the tubulopathy probably drug-related. The cord and nerve mechanism stays unproven because the switch and the metabolic treatment were given together. Report the reaction and use teach-back.

PHASES (3):
- admission: history, examination, decision 1, and the MRI, blood and urine orders, whose results show as pending here.
- workup: opens when the history, examination and localise objectives are complete; the localise objective includes the MRI, blood and urine orders. It holds the results plus the MRI and neurophysiology reports as records, decisions 2–5 and the treatment.
- followup: opens once all 5 decisions are answered. It holds the outcome record and is not learner-switchable.

DECISIONS (5, 4–5 options each, content-named ids, no key uniquely longest in either language): lesion-site, tubular-pattern, antiviral-plan, bone-plan, causality-followup. Each opens before the result that answers it: the MRI report answers decision 1; the outcome answers decisions 2–5.

INTERVENTIONS (15):
- The report's management: switch-to-entecavir, phosphate-vitd.
- Today's steps: switch-to-taf (doseSpec 25 mg PO), hepatology-consult, nephrology-consult, pharmacist-review, falls-prevention (NICE NG249 2025), explain-plan, adr-report.
- Tempting wrong or historical steps:
  - stop-all-antivirals: risk high, critical true.
  - epidural-injection: risk high, critical true.
  - switch-to-tdf, continue-adefovir, nsaid, spinal-manipulation: moderate, critical false.
  - Each has a harm text naming its guidance.

RUBRIC: 15 items, 14 deterministic with total weight 34, plus an examiner-judged Calgary–Cambridge/teach-back item specific to Mr Shi. The three critical items are acts:
- rb-cord-imaging: spine MRI, blood and urine ordered in admission.
- rb-switch-in-time: entecavir or TAF given whenIndicated — in workup, after the blood and urine reads, before the outcome.
- rb-no-harm: safety item; its scoredWhen lists all 6 harmful interventions plus decisions 1 and 3.

STAFF: Dr Fang, internal medicine attending (Socratic, PEARLS, revealsDiagnosis false); Nurse Tang (ISBAR); Dr Qiu, hepatology; Dr Yan, nephrology; Pharmacist Wen, clinical pharmacist. All pseudonyms.

HISTORY: 22 items (8 required) in his own words; 14 are unknown or teaching items, each said in character.

MATCHER: 47 test utterances, 3 of them negatives; 47/47 pass.

MEASURED SCORES (core assess):
- Reference path: 34/34 (100 %).
- Doing nothing: 0/31, and the case cannot be finished.
- Wrong first answer at every decision: 21/34 (62 %). Wrong first at decision 1, 2 or 3 alone: 91 %; at decision 4 or 5 alone: 94 %.
- Reference plus stop-all-antivirals or plus an epidural: 31/34, and the safety outcome FAILS.
- Reference plus TDF, continued adefovir, diclofenac or manipulation: 31/34, flagged, safety outcome passes.
- Switch made only after reading the outcome: 30/34, rb-switch-in-time missed.
- TAF instead of entecavir: 100 %.

- Course: switch to entecavir with nutritional/bone-metabolism support; phosphate improved over weeks; walking normal at 5 months; tubular markers fell markedly, some still abnormal → `outcome` record in followup.
- Article title (adefovir dipivoxil–associated Fanconi syndrome with myelopathy and peripheral neuropathy) → provenance.citation, the outcome record and the debrief.
- Inpatient setting, lying, gown → kept.
- 1.0.0 unknowns:
  - allergies, family, exposures, function, red flags, baseline → unknown items `allergies`, `family`, `alcohol`, `diet-weight`, `daily-life`, `bone-pain`, `hands`, `bowels`, `other-meds`, `hbv-history`, `kidney-monitoring`, all said in character.

CONTRADICTIONS AND TRANSLATION DIFFERENCES (kept in neutral wording and listed in To verify):
- The neurophysiology record says 双下肢…阻滞 in Chinese (both lower limbs, "blocked") and "impaired lower-limb deep sensory conduction" in English. Rendered as "Impaired (blocked) conduction … of both lower limbs".
- 紧束感 in Chinese vs "tight band-like" in English. The patient says "tight, as if bound"; clinical text says "band-like".

INFERENCES (derived, not new):
- The combined 1.0.0 record "MRI and neurophysiology" is split into two reports, with "mild degenerative change" placed with the MRI.
- Unit conversions: creatinine ≈ 1.35 mg/dL; phosphate ≈ 1.15 mg/dL; urate ≈ 2.05 mg/dL; calcium ≈ 7.9 mg/dL; glucose ≈ 81 mg/dL.
- eGFR ≈ 59 mL/min/1.73 m² by CKD-EPI 2021 — a single value that likely overestimates function in cirrhosis.
- Alpha-1 microglobulin ≈ 20 × and NAG 4.5 × their upper reference limits.
- Back pain and walking difficulty began about 4 years into adefovir (5.5 − 1.5).
- Low phosphate and low urate follow 1.0.0's own reading. Hypocalcaemia is NOT asserted, because albumin is unknown.

WHAT STAYS UNKNOWN:
- Vital signs, weight, height.
- HBV DNA, HBeAg, liver function, albumin, INR, platelets, Child-Pugh class and whether the cirrhosis was compensated.
- Adefovir dose and interval, earlier hepatitis B drugs (lamivudine) or resistance, and whether kidneys and phosphate were monitored.
- Potassium, bicarbonate, magnesium, ALP, PTH, vitamin D, urine phosphate, urine pH, urine amino acids, and the grades of glycosuria and proteinuria.
- Neurology: cervical cord imaging, cord signal, nerve-conduction details behind "peripheral neuropathy", B12, copper, HIV, syphilis, HTLV-1; sensory examination (vibration, joint position, sensory level), upper-limb power, bowel function.
- History: allergies, alcohol, diet and weight, family history, daily function, other medicines.
- Treatment: entecavir dose, what the supportive treatment contained, any values after the switch, which tubular markers stayed abnormal, follow-up beyond 5 months.
safetyFixes: Antiviral key rewritten: stop adefovir and switch the same day — entecavir if he never had lamivudine, otherwise tenofovir alafenamide — never pause treatment in cirrhosis. 1.0.0's key did not say to switch at once or warn against stopping.

Stopping adefovir with no replacement (stop-all-antivirals) is now a critical intervention (risk high, critical true). Its harm cites the Hepsera label 2018 (up to 25 % hepatitis exacerbations after stopping, higher decompensation risk in cirrhosis, deaths reported) and EASL 2025 (no NA discontinuation in advanced liver disease before HBsAg loss).

Preconditions named in the key, feedback, consultants and reference path: HBV DNA and liver function/clotting/platelets before choosing drug and dose. Entecavir is 0.5 mg (compensated) or 1 mg (decompensated) on an empty stomach, adjusted below a creatinine clearance of 50 mL/min. TAF is not recommended in Child-Pugh B/C. The lamivudine history decides between entecavir and TAF.

Switching to TDF is flagged as contraindicated (critical false): it shares the proximal tubular toxicity (EASL 2025 prefers TAF or entecavir in hypophosphataemia or renal insufficiency; the Chinese 2022 guideline advises against ADV or TDF in kidney disease).
Continuing adefovir at a renally adjusted interval is flagged as contraindicated (critical false). Chinese 2022 guideline: once the reaction is confirmed, stop the drug, switch and treat.

A lumbar epidural steroid injection for presumed disc disease is a critical intervention (risk high, critical true). It targets the wrong level for a cord lesion; with cirrhosis, splenomegaly and platelets/clotting unrecorded it risks an epidural haematoma and paraplegia; NICE NG59 2016 does not recommend spinal injections for back pain.

NSAID (diclofenac) for the back pain is flagged (critical false). The adefovir label lists NSAIDs among nephrotoxic co-medications; NICE NG59 says to weigh GI, liver and cardio-renal toxicity; he has cirrhosis with varices and an injured tubule.

The historical step — more massage and spinal manipulation for a 'disc' — is flagged as contraindicated in an undiagnosed myelopathy (NICE NG59: exclude specific causes first; manual therapy only for non-specific low back pain, within a package that includes exercise).
Localisation key names MRI of the CERVICAL and thoracic cord, because bilateral Hoffmann signs point to the cervical level or above; the report's MRI names only the thoracic level.

Bone decision teaches osteomalacia versus osteoporosis. Zoledronic acid is contraindicated in hypocalcaemia and below a creatinine clearance of 35 mL/min (Reclast label), and the total calcium of 1.97 mmol/L cannot be read without albumin. Phosphate is replaced orally with active vitamin D after albumin, magnesium, PTH and vitamin D are checked.

1.0.0's hindsight-creditable critical item (a decision answered after reading the outcome) is replaced by acts done in time: cord MRI with blood and urine ordered in the admission phase; the antiviral switch inside an indicatedWhen window (workup, after the results are read, before the outcome is read); plus a critical avoided-harm item.

Falls precautions added (NICE NG249 2025): he needs support to walk. Also added: adverse-drug-reaction reporting (2011 provisions) and teach-back that he must never stop the hepatitis B tablets himself.
guidelines: European Association for the Study of the Liver — EASL Clinical Practice Guidelines on the management of hepatitis B virus infection, J Hepatol 2025;83(2):502–583, doi:10.1016/j.jhep.2025.03.018. Checked online: full text downloaded and read. Confirmed: TAF preferred over TDF in hypophosphataemia or renal insufficiency, entecavir the alternative; entecavir after adefovir only if lamivudine was not used; creatinine alone may not reflect tubular damage; no NA stop in advanced liver disease before HBsAg loss; HBV DNA every 3–6 months until response; switch TDF to entecavir or TAF on tubulopathy or hypophosphataemia.

中华医学会肝病学分会、中华医学会感染病学分会 — 慢性乙型肝炎防治指南（2022年版）, 中华肝脏病杂志 2022;30(12):1309–1331. Checked online: full text of the reprint (实用肝脏病杂志 2023) read. Confirmed: recommendation 28 (B1); patients on adefovir or TDF who develop kidney or bone disease switch to entecavir or TAF; monitor creatinine and phosphate; once the reaction is confirmed, stop, switch and treat. Cited without DOI because the 中华肝脏病杂志 DOI could not be verified.

European Association for the Study of the Liver — EASL Clinical Practice Guidelines for the management of patients with decompensated cirrhosis, J Hepatol 2018;69(2):406–460. HRS-AKI criteria (no nephrotoxic drugs; no parenchymal disease such as proteinuria > 500 mg/day) checked online through secondary summaries.

Gilead Sciences — HEPSERA (adefovir dipivoxil) prescribing information, revised 12/2018. Checked online: label text read. Confirmed §5.1 (exacerbations after stopping, up to 25 %; cirrhosis; fatalities), §5.2 (delayed nephrotoxicity; NSAIDs named as nephrotoxic co-medication) and §6.4 (Fanconi syndrome, proximal tubulopathy, hypophosphataemia, osteomalacia with bone pain and fractures).

Bristol-Myers Squibb — BARACLUDE (entecavir) prescribing information, 2019. Dosing (0.5 mg naive and compensated; 1 mg lamivudine-refractory or decompensated; empty stomach; adjust below CrCl 50) checked online through FDA label excerpts.
Gilead Sciences — VEMLIDY (tenofovir alafenamide) prescribing information, revised 03/2024. Checked online: 25 mg once daily with food; not recommended in Child-Pugh B/C; no adjustment at CrCl ≥ 15.

NICE NG59 — Low back pain and sciatica in over 16s: assessment and management, 2016. Checked online through search: the NICE page returned 403. Confirmed rec 1.3.1 (no spinal injections for low back pain), the manual-therapy recommendation (amended July 2026), and the NSAID caution about GI, liver and cardio-renal toxicity.
NICE NG249 — Falls: assessment and prevention in older people and in people 50 and over at higher risk, 29 April 2025. Checked online.

Uppsala Monitoring Centre — The use of the WHO-UMC system for standardised case causality assessment. 'Probable' = plausible time relationship, unlikely other cause, reasonable response to withdrawal, rechallenge not required. Checked online through reproduced tables; edition year not fixed.
中华人民共和国卫生部 — 药品不良反应报告和监测管理办法（卫生部令第81号）, issued 2011-05-04, effective 2011-07-01. Checked online.
Novartis — RECLAST (zoledronic acid) prescribing information. Contraindicated in hypocalcaemia and with creatinine clearance < 35 mL/min; checked online.
Teaching frameworks used without online check: Calgary–Cambridge guide, PEARLS debriefing, ISBAR handover, teach-back, CKD-EPI 2021 equation (derived eGFR only).
